title: PromotionUniV2_Eth._legB swaps the whole contract ETH balance while receive() is open: stray/donated ETH folds into the next pooler's buy and rescueETH is front-runnable (Law-3 footgun)
crossRef: F-01-044 (story-044 faithfulness record for the same whole-balance ETH sweep)
description: Leg B of pool() first unwraps this call's USDC into ETH via swapExactTokensForETH, then reads ethBal = address(this).balance (L342) and swaps the ENTIRE contract ETH balance into promotion via swapExactETHForTokens{value: ethBal} — not the amounts[1] output the swap just returned. receive() (L400) is open and unguarded, so any third party (donation, coinbase transfer, or ETH stranded by a prior partial/failed Leg B not yet rescueETH'd) can pre-fund ETH onto the contract. On the NEXT authorized pool(), that stray ETH folds into whichever pooler calls next, buying promotion tokens at THAT keeper's off-chain floors (minPromoOut/minLP) and mis-attributing the donation to them. rescueETH (L393) is the intended sweep, but a pooler can front-run it.
impact: No value at risk to the protocol or third parties. Donated/stray ETH is irreversibly converted to promotionToken and added to protocol-owned phUSD/promotion LP (withdrawable only via owner rescueERC20). Tier-3 INV-4 confirmed the value can NEVER route to a third party. The only party who can lose value is a self-harming donor who voluntarily sends ETH to the open receive(). No revert/DoS path (extra ETH only raises promotion-out, easing minPromoOut; the uint112 reserve overflow needs an infeasible >uint112 donation). The reportable substance is the surprising state-handling / value-misattribution consequence plus the rescueETH front-running timing hazard, not theft.
attackPath: 1. _legB reads ethBal = address(this).balance and swaps the ENTIRE contract ETH balance (not just this call's USDC->ETH output).
2. Open receive() (L400) lets any third party pre-fund ETH onto the contract.
3. On the NEXT authorized pool(), that stray ETH folds into whichever pooler calls next, buying promotion at that keeper's floors and mis-attributing the donation to them.
4. Net: donor loses ETH; protocol gains LP. No theft, no third-party profit, no DoS.
c4Justification: NOT High: no direct or indirect theft/loss — value is conserved into protocol-owned LP (Tier-3 INV-4). NOT Medium: no protocol-function/availability impact and no conditional value-leak away from the protocol (the flow is protocol-POSITIVE). ABOVE QA: a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that (a) any third party's stray ETH folds into the next pool at that keeper's floors and (b) a pooler can front-run rescueETH — a non-obvious Law-3 footgun with a demonstrated state-handling / value-misattribution consequence and safe-config guidance. => Low (incorrect/surprising state handling + in-scope operational hazard), consistent with the ledger's other non-obvious footgun Lows (L-10 deploy-config, L-11 batch-floor staleness, L-12 pause-custody gap). The accidental-send variant is additionally C4 known-invalid ("user input mistake"), which caps the reportable substance to the footgun/state-handling framing.
recommendation: Sweep stray ETH (rescueETH, L393) before authorizing a pool() if it must not enter LP; document that the whole-balance sweep is intentional so a future maintainer does not 'fix' it into a leak. Optionally swap only the leg's own amounts[1] output rather than the whole balance.
safeConfigGuidance: rescueETH stray ETH before opening a pool(); document the whole-balance sweep as intentional. A pooler can front-run rescueETH, so do not rely on it as a race-free escape.
